title: Cost Model API: audit log reads (estimate/explain) w/ tenant + actor metadata
author: Felix Schneider
description: Motivation: Console and Optimize will be calling the Cost Model API for per-tenant cost breakdowns. Security requested auditability for any read access that returns customer-level cost breakdowns (including actor identity + tenant scoping) before we expand rollout. This PR adds structured audit events for cost-model read endpoints (estimate + explain), enforces consistent tenant/actor extraction at the gateway boundary, and introduces redaction rules so sensitive payload fields are not logged. Scope: (1) emit audit events for POST /v1/cost-model:estimate and POST /v1/cost-model:explain, (2) include tenant_id, environment, region, actor_type, actor_id (when available), and request_id/trace_id, (3) add a conservative allowlist of fields for request/response metadata (no prompts, no raw token sequences, no per-request customer identifiers beyond tenant_id), (4) add tests to prevent accidental logging of request/response bodies, and (5) document security review notes and open questions for follow-ups. Security review notes (requested by SecEng): - We treat cost breakdown as customer-sensitive operational data (not billing source-of-truth, but still sensitive). - Audit events must be emitted on successful reads and on authorization failures (attempted access) with minimal context. - Do not log prompts, user content, or model outputs; do not log raw token counts at per-request granularity if it risks reconstructing usage patterns. - Retention: follows existing audit pipeline defaults (90d searchable + 1y cold storage) managed outside this service; this PR tags events with data_classification="customer_sensitive" for downstream routing. - Access: only Security/Compliance + limited SRE oncall breakglass can query raw audit stream; product/eng dashboards must use aggregated metrics. API behavior: no functional changes for clients other than adding an X-Redwood-Audit-Id response header (opaque) to help correlate support escalations with audit records. Implementation details: - New audit event types: cost_model.estimate.read and cost_model.explain.read (and cost_model.*.read_denied for authz failures). - Actor extraction: uses existing gateway auth context; supports service-to-service (actor_type=service, actor_id=spiffe), user tokens (actor_type=user, actor_id=sub), and internal tooling (actor_type=employee, actor_id=okta_id) where present. - Tenant extraction: from required x-redwood-tenant header (service-to-service) or token claim tenant_id; we emit tenant_id="unknown" only for 4xx pre-auth requests and explicitly mark missing_tenant=true. - Redaction: audit payload includes only schema version requested/resolved, endpoint, model_id (if provided), deployment_mode, and high-level response status; no request params beyond allowlist. Changed areas: services/cost-model-service (middleware + handlers), gateway/audit (new event schema + redaction helpers), authz/context (actor/tenant normalization), docs/security (event field reference). Test plan: unit tests for event emission + redaction; integration test hitting estimate/explain with mock auth contexts; canary in staging to verify events appear in audit stream with correct fields. Release notes: Adds audit logging for Cost Model API reads; no customer-visible behavior change besides opaque correlation header. Follow-ups: (a) add rate-limited sampling for high-QPS endpoints if audit pipeline backpressure is observed, (b) decide whether to include request "purpose" (console_page vs optimize_sweep) as an enumerated field once clients stabilize, (c) add dashboards for audit volume anomalies (separate PR).
commits: audit: introduce cost-model read event types + schema v1
cost-model-service: emit audit events for estimate/explain success paths
gateway: normalize actor + tenant fields for audit payloads
security: add redaction allowlist + regression tests for body logging
docs: add audit event field reference + examples
snippet: New event payload (illustrative; actual logging is structured): event_type=cost_model.estimate.read tenant_id=tnt_3f2a... actor_type=service actor_id=spiffe://redwood/optimize request_id=req_01HP... trace_id=4f2b... endpoint=/v1/cost-model:estimate scm_version_requested=v1 scm_version_resolved=v1 model_id=llama-3.1-70b deployment_mode=hosted status=200 data_classification=customer_sensitive
review_conversation: Kevin Osei: Please confirm we never log request/response bodies (including assumptions/confidence arrays) even at debug. Felix Schneider: Confirmed; audit middleware uses an explicit allowlist and ignores handler payload. Added a regression test that fails if body keys appear in emitted event map. Dr. Aisha Rahman: For denied requests, we need an attempted access event with minimal fields. Also ensure tenant_id is not derived from untrusted client headers if we have a token claim. Felix Schneider: Added cost_model.*.read_denied events for authz failures (403/401) with endpoint, actor_type, actor_id (if present), and tenant_id from verified auth context; header-only tenant is marked missing_tenant=true unless validated. Marcus Lin: Redaction helper should live in gateway-audit, not in cost-model-service, to keep policy centralized. Felix Schneider: Moved redaction + schema into packages/gateway-audit; service only calls emitAuditEvent() with a typed payload. Priya Natarajan: Any perf impact? These endpoints may be on the Console critical path. Felix Schneider: Emission is async/non-blocking; failures are swallowed after incrementing a counter (existing audit pipeline client behavior). Added a micro-benchmark in tests showing <0.2ms overhead p95 on handler path. Jordan Lee: Add an opaque correlation id in response headers for support. Felix Schneider: Added X-Redwood-Audit-Id with event_id; documented in internal docs only. Approvals: Kevin Osei approved, Dr. Aisha Rahman approved, Marcus Lin approved, Priya Natarajan approved.
final_ci_summary: All checks passed; merged to main. Post-merge action: enable audit events in staging canary (feature flag audit.cost_model_reads=true) and confirm downstream ingestion before expanding tenant rollout.
